reasoning: Both attempts meet the core requirements and check RemoveBlock's argument properly. B keeps per-player state more robust: the Destroying hook calls forgetBlock, state is created on PlayerAdded, and late events after a player leaves are ignored. Its comments also explain why the code is written as it is. A's counts can drift if a block is destroyed some other way, and a late request can recreate entries for a player who has left. B's StyLua failure is a real defect but a trivial one to fix, so B wins narrowly.

criteria.note: Creates both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder, enforces the cap and the 0.1 s throttle, keeps removal owner-only and cleans up on leave; but if a block is destroyed some other way its count drifts, and a request arriving after PlayerRemoving can recreate that player's state.
onRemoveBlock checks typeof Instance, then ownerByBlock[block] == player, then IsA BasePart before Destroy; it also checks typeof(result) == "Vector3" after validate.
The only real comment explains why the throttle timestamp is set only after the check passes, which is a useful why; '-- seconds' gives the unit.
The throttle comment spans two lines and could probably be one; otherwise there's no banner or boilerplate.
No comment mentions history or the request.

criteria.criterion: Reuse, scope, typed and passes checks
criteria.note: Uses BlockTypes.STYLES and PlacementRules.BLOCK_SIZE/validate, is typed under --!strict, and passes every check.

forgetBlock plus the Destroying hook keep ownerOf, blocksOf and blockCount consistent however a block is destroyed, state is set up on PlayerAdded (including players already in game), and requests from departed players are ignored.
RemoveBlock checks typeof Instance, IsA BasePart and ownerOf[part] == player before Destroy; the only trust is the result :: Vector3 cast after validate succeeds.

The comments explain real decisions: ownership is kept server-side so a client can't claim a block by editing an attribute, the attribute exists only for the client/UI, and the Destroying hook covers other destroy paths.
All single-line, though the PLACE_COOLDOWN comment partly restates the name.
No comment mentions history or the request.
